function: Learned RIS phase-shift design for joint sensing and communication beamforming in a RIS-aided ISAC system; the transmit beamformer is closed-form (p. 1-3).
system: 8-antenna ISAC base station, one single-antenna user, one sensed target, passive reflecting RIS with 32 elements; frequency band not stated (p. 1, p. 4).
method: Lightweight CNN (IBF-Net, depthwise-pointwise convolutions) trained with unsupervised learning; loss from channel correlation and sensing channel gain (p. 3).
data_channel: Simulated Rician channels similar to [11]; 500,000 generated training samples and 100 test samples (p. 4).
test_conditions: Same Rician setting for training and testing (100 test samples); RIS size N, power and threshold are varied, with no stated reuse of a model across settings (p. 4).
baselines: Non-learned only: AO, SDR-based alternating optimization [4], and Rotation, subspace rotation [7]; no learned baseline compared (p. 4).
metrics: Sensing SNR, communication SNR against the user threshold, training loss, and average running time per sample (p. 4-5).
complexity: Operation count 1184N^2+576(N^2-N)+2048N^2 log2 N+6M, O(N^2+N^2 log2 N+M); runtime 3.9 ms versus AO 6.61e3 ms at N=32 (p. 5).
openness: Code released at https://github.com/Yejacky456/DL-Beamforming-RIS-ISAC; no dataset link (p. 1).
q1_support: p. 4: "All channels are characterized as Rician channels similar to [11]"; a custom Rician simulator, with no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "100 samples are used to evaluate the generalization capability of the model"; these are held-out samples of the same Rician setting, and no unseen scenario is reported.
q3_support: p. 4: "we compare it against two representative algorithms"; both (AO, Rotation) are non-learned, and no earlier learned method for the same function is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "the running times of the proposed method and the benchmarks are shown in Table II"; the same section gives the operation count and the order O(N^2 + N^2 log2 N + M).
notes: Area 5 over 3: the learned RIS phases serve a joint sensing and communication beamforming problem in an ISAC system (p. 1). The transmit beamformer is the closed-form Theorem 1 (p. 2). The network input is 4xNxN and its depth depends on N (p. 3), so the sweep of N in Fig. 4 (p. 4) is not stated as testing a model on a size it was not trained for. Learned works [8]-[12] appear only in the introduction (p. 1).
